Welcome to the Department of Mathematical Sciences at Durham
Mathematical Sciences at Durham offers a unique blend of high-quality teaching and research in Applied & Computational Mathematics, Mathematical & Theoretical Physics, Pure Mathematics, Probability, and Statistics. We pride ourselves on combining world-leading research with a dedication to the learning experience of our undergraduate and postgraduate students.
Our curriculum and degree structure is monitored and regularly updated to provide students with the best possible mathematical and general skills, equipping them for a rapidly changing professional environment. Our degree portfolio has recently been enriched to offer the possibility of a year in industry and a new route in statistics that will give interested students practical experience of problem-solving in a commercial environment.

Durham is University of the Year 2026
We are The Times and The Sunday Times Good University Guide University of the Year 2026. We are also joint runner-up University of the Year for Graduate Employment and ranked third overall, up two places from last year.
Study with us
Find out more about the undergraduate and postgraduate programmes we offer at the Department of Mathematical Sciences.
Undergraduate study
We offer various undergraduate courses which allow choice from a wide spectrum of pure mathematics, applied mathematics (including mathematical physics) and statistics.
Postgraduate study
We currently offer three taught postgraduate degrees which offer a gateway to a variety of careers and a natural pathway to a PhD.
QS World University Rankings 2027: Durham ranks 85th, up 9 places
Our global reputation for employability reflects the quality and real-world relevance of our education and research. Ranked 85th overall, we are also among the world’s top 50 for Employer Reputation and placed joint 24th for Sustainability.

Research in the Department of Mathematical Sciences is organised into a number of research groups. We are also members of various scientific networks, addressing a wide selection of topics from the mathematics of climate change to geometric group theory.

Europe’s largest solar telescope reaches major milestone with Durham involvement
Our scientists are part of an international team behind plans for Europe’s largest solar telescope – which has just reached a new milestone.
Global research
Department of Mathematical Sciences hosts landmark MEGA conference
Mathematicians working at the computational forefront of algebra, geometry, and combinatorics gathered in Durham earlier this month for MEGA 2026 (Effective Methods in Algebraic Geometry), one of the world's leading conferences in computational algebraic geometry. The event, held from 6–10 July, marked the 19th edition of the prestigious biennial conference series and only the second time it has taken place in the UK.
Global research
Durham Symposium strengthens UK–Japan research links
About 50 researchers from the UK, Japan, Mexico, China, and across Europe visited Durham University from 13–17 July for the Durham Symposium on Metric Geometry, Analysis and Probability. The five-day symposium, hosted by the Department of Mathematical Sciences, brought together established and early-career researchers to share ideas, showcase recent advances, and identify new opportunities for future collaboration.

Collingwood Lecture 2026: Professor Don Zagier explores the oldest and newest problems in mathematics
The Department of Mathematical Sciences was delighted to welcome Professor Don Zagier (Max Planck Institute for Mathematics, Bonn, and the International Centre for Theoretical Physics, Trieste) for the 2025/26 Collingwood Lecture, held on 11 June 2026.
Global research
Whitley Bay beach becomes a giant mathematical canvas for Beach Spectres
Members of the public, volunteers, and mathematicians came together at Whitley Bay on 6 and 7 June to create a remarkable large-scale artwork in the sand, inspired by one of the most exciting recent discoveries in geometry. The Beach Spectres event invited participants to help build an aperiodic tiling on the beach using large stampers shaped like the Spectre monotile.

Exploring mathematical biology: Durham Symposium and Pascal Public Lecture
The Durham Symposium on Mathematical Biology brought together around 100 researchers from the UK, Europe and North America to explore mathematical approaches to biological problems. As part of the programme, Professor Philip Maini FRS delivered the Pascal Public Lecture, demonstrating how mathematics can generate insights into biology, ecology and medicine.

Building connections: Postdoctoral meetups in Mathematical Sciences
Regular meetups are helping postdoctoral researchers in our Department build connections, share experiences, and feel more at home in Durham.
From informal lunches and walks around the city to day trips across the region, the meetups offer opportunities to get to know colleagues at a similar career stage, exchange practical advice, and develop friendships beyond the working environment.
